rateLimits.note: Without an API key, per IP address; with an api_key: 10 requests a second for all activity from that key (scope key).
Without an API key; with an api-key header: 10 requests a second.

provenance.notes: Operations: eutils = https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/, datasets = https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/v2/. Read 2026-11-10: NCBI Insights (E-utilities: 3 requests/s per IP without a key, 10/s per key with one; limits count request starts, concurrent requests allowed; more on request to eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), NCBI Datasets API-keys page (5 rps by default, 10 rps with a key), NCBI policies (no restriction on use or distribution of the molecular data, though submitters may claim patent, copyright or other rights; a service built on E-utilities must make the NCBI Disclaimer and Copyright notice evident to its users). Live headers: X-RateLimit-Limit 3 on eutils, 5 on datasets (keyless). The E-utilities book (www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25497) sits behind a reCAPTCHA check and could not be read: its tool and email parameters (identify the application, registered with NCBI; a blocked IP is restored once they are registered) come from search excerpts of it; userAgent.required stands for those parameters, not a User-Agent header. No data licence is named (NCBI data is US government work, rights of submitters aside).
